slides.title: Pudu Robotics Unveils PuduFM 1.0 and PuduAgent
slides.tldr: NEW HUMANOID AND EMBODIED AI SYSTEMS
slides.highlight: The introduction of PuduFM 1.0 and PuduAgent advances humanoid and embodied AI systems, providing relevant insights for RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Is Telehealth Better Used to Treat Patients or Help Other Physicians Treat Patients? An Agent-Based Modeling Study of Healthcare Provision
slides.highlight: This study uses agent-based modeling to analyze how physician-to-physician versus physician-to-patient telehealth affects clinical outcomes and system utilization, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: Telehealth is more cost-effective for toxicologist-physician consultations than for direct toxicologist-patient care.
card.key_idea: An agent-based model simulating medical toxicology care to compare health outcomes and costs across physician-physician, physician-patient, and poison control center access points.
card.evaluation: Simulated 1,000 patients and 100 physicians across 100 runs; results were validated against existing empirical cost-savings data for poison control centers.
card.limitation: Relies on simulated data and an incomplete model that assumes perfect in-hospital diagnostic accuracy and single medical problems per patient.

slides.title: Modelling Opinion Dynamics at Scale with Deep MARL
slides.highlight: This research uses multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate opinion dynamics and conformity in large social networks, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Deep MARL models opinion dynamics to show how conformity in large social networks promotes misinformation.
card.key_idea: A GPU-accelerated consensus and truth-finding game using general-sum other-play MARL and a learned attention layer to recover agent importance from graph topology.
card.evaluation: Validated on a Bluesky network subset; compared large social media networks against small hunter-gatherer networks regarding collective accuracy and conformity.

slides.title: From Shortcuts to Reasoning: Robust Post-Training of Theory of Mind with Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: ROBUST THEORY OF MIND VIA REINFORCEMENT LEARNING
slides.highlight: This work introduces Thinking-RFT to improve Theory of Mind (ToM) capabilities and robustness against shortcuts, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of inferring partner intent via ToM.

card.one_liner: Thinking-RFT improves Theory of Mind reasoning in LLMs by overcoming dataset shortcuts via verifiable rewards.
card.key_idea: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) using Group Relative Preference Optimization (GRPO) with explicit reasoning chains and verifiable rewards to ground models in causal factors rather than spurious correlations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four shortcut-free datasets (OpenToM, ToMATO, MMToM, MuMA-ToM) against SFT and zero-shot; Thinking-RFT showed +6% gain over SFT and superior OOD generalization.
card.limitation: Performance gains are negated if training data contains shortcuts, which can lead to illogical reasoning and poor generalization.

slides.title: Personality Anchoring for Social Simulation: Linking Personality, Social Behavior, and Interaction Success with LLM Agents
slides.tldr: PERSONALITY ANCHORING FOR LLM SOCIAL SIMULATION
slides.highlight: This research introduces personality anchoring to simulate how dyadic personality traits influence social behavior and goal achievement, supporting MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: High dyadic Agreeableness significantly increases shared goal achievement in LLM-based social simulations via cooperative strategies.
card.key_idea: Personality anchoring leverages LLMs' internal knowledge of well-known characters to simulate personality-consistent behavior without explicit trait prompting, using a structured taxonomy of human goals.
card.evaluation: 1,010 conversations across 7 goal categories. Evaluated via LLM-as-a-judge for goal achievement and ICC for consistency (0.89). Results were replicated with Mistral Large.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM-as-a-judge scoring and pre-existing character knowledge, which may introduce stereotypical biases and lack cultural diversity.

slides.title: UBTECH launches UWORLD U1 humanoid robot companions
slides.highlight: The launch of UWORLD U1 humanoid robot companions is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Personalized and Robust Proactive Robot Assistance with Uncertainty-Guided LLM Reasoning
slides.tldr: PROACTIVE ROBOT ASSISTANCE VIA UNCERTAINTY-GUIDED LLM REASONING
slides.highlight: The GLOBE framework improves proactive robot assistance in noisy household environments by combining Markov models with LLM reasoning. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied AI.

card.one_liner: GLOBE uses n-gram Markov models and selective LLM reasoning for robust, proactive household object prediction.
card.key_idea: Combines lightweight n-gram Markov models for temporal patterns with an LLM that is selectively triggered via a confidence threshold to resolve prediction uncertainty.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HOMER+ and a new HOMER-Noise dataset (simulating human/pet/toddler disturbances) using F1-scores; compared against SLaTe-PRO and STOT.
card.limitation: Inference latency is significantly higher than baselines due to external LLM API calls.

slides.title: What Is My Robot Thinking? Design Considerations for Transparent and Trustworthy Shared Autonomy
slides.highlight: This research explores how interface transparency and feedback modalities improve intent alignment and coordination in shared autonomy, supporting MOSAIC's goal of aligning human-AI intent.

card.one_liner: Interface-level transparency in shared autonomy improves goal alignment and reduces corrective inputs, regardless of modality.
card.key_idea: Evaluated visual vs. auditory feedback and sparse vs. rich information richness on a fixed vision-based shared autonomy controller to isolate interface effects on coordination and trust.
card.evaluation: User study (N=25) across two manipulation tasks (shelving, sorting) using ANOVA, Wilcoxon signed-rank, and chi-square tests. Results show visual feedback is preferred over auditory.
card.limitation: Full belief disclosure did not consistently improve trust or alignment, and rich feedback can overwhelm users in complex, cluttered environments.

slides.title: Safe, Fluent and Acceptable Motion Generation and Execution for Human--Robot Interaction in Manufacturing Environments
slides.tldr: SOCIALLY-AWARE MOTION CONTROL FOR HUMAN-ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This research explores integrating social-aware motion control and psycho-cognitive perspectives into robot behavior to improve social acceptability. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A motion control framework that generates socially-aware robot behaviors by modulating velocity and interaction distance.
card.key_idea: An MPC framework using separating-plane optimization and LSTM-based human motion prediction to implement four distinct behaviors based on maximum velocity and interaction distance parameters.
card.evaluation: Validated via a user study with 111 non-experts using NASA-TLX and 10 bipolar adjective scales; results showed significant impacts on social perception.
card.limitation: Interaction distance had minimal significant effect on most perceptual dimensions compared to the strong influence of velocity profiles.

slides.title: Uncertainty-Aware Intention Prediction for Human-to-Robot Assembly Teleoperation
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework for intention prediction and mistake detection in assembly tasks, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on human-AI intent alignment and skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: A framework for robot assembly intention prediction using human-to-robot transfer learning and uncertainty-aware correction.
card.key_idea: Combines MS-TCN++ pre-trained on human data, conformal prediction for statistical uncertainty guarantees, and selective VLM-guided correction for low-confidence segments.
card.evaluation: Tested on 22 action classes; human-to-robot fine-tuning improved Edit score from 70.50 to 80.70 using only 16 robot demonstrations.
card.limitation: VLM correction adds latency hindering real-time use; results are limited to a single platform and task.

slides.title: Voting Protocols as Coordination Mechanisms for Role-Constrained Multi-Agent Tutoring Systems
slides.highlight: This research explores how different voting protocols shape coordination and collective decision-making among role-specialized agents, providing insights into how ADAM-CHAT can manage conflicting agent interventions to align with team goals.

card.one_liner: Voting protocols actively shape coordination and decision outcomes among role-specialized multi-agent tutoring systems.
card.key_idea: Four pedagogical agents (scaffolding, misconception, motivation, metacognition) propose interventions, undergo a deliberation/revision phase, and use different voting rules to select a final response.
card.evaluation: 1,200 simulated interactions across SciQ and HumanEval benchmarks using six learner personas; measured via judge scores, code execution, and coordination diagnostics.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM-based simulated students and judges, which may not reflect real human learner behavior or psychological realism.

slides.title: Distilling LLM Reasoning into an Interpretable Policy Tree for Human-AI Collaboration
slides.tldr: DISTILLING LLM REASONING INTO INTERPRETABLE POLICY TREES
slides.highlight: The proposed Co-pi-tree method distills LLM reasoning into executable policy trees for human-AI collaboration, demonstrating improved rewards and reduced latency in Overcooked-AI. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on adaptive AI teammates and evaluation via Overcooked-AI.

card.one_liner: Co-pi-tree distills LLM reasoning into an interpretable policy tree to improve human-AI collaboration efficiency.
card.key_idea: A closed-loop method distilling LLM reasoning into executable partner-prediction and action-selection trees, iteratively refined using natural language summaries of interaction feedback.
card.evaluation: Tested in Overcooked-AI; showed 35.4% higher average reward, 77.7% fewer LLM queries, and 97.1% lower latency than baselines.

slides.title: Titans-as-a-Layer: Test-Time Memory for Conversational Speech Emotion Recognition
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Memory-as-a-Layer adapter to capture dialogue history and emotional context, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: Introduces a plug-and-play memory adapter to capture dialogue context for conversational speech emotion recognition.
card.key_idea: A Memory-as-a-Layer (MAL) adapter using Titans-style neural memory provides audio-token-aligned residual updates to frozen LALMs, trained sequentially after LoRA task adaptation.
card.evaluation: Tested on IEMOCAP, MELD, and MultiDialog using Qwen2-Audio, Audio Flamingo 3, and Ultravox-v0.4; showed consistent improvements in WA, UA, and WF1.
card.limitation: Further validation across more backbone-dataset combinations and comparisons with other memory architectures are needed.

slides.title: Impedance MPC for Physical Human-Robot Interaction: Predictive Disturbance Rejection with Joint-Limit Safety
slides.tldr: IMPROVED COMPLIANT SAFETY AND ACCURACY IN pHRI
slides.highlight: This work introduces a two-layer Impedance MPC that achieves zero steady-state error under sustained human force while ensuring joint-limit safety, supporting the development of embodied social robots in RwB.

card.one_liner: A two-layer Impedance MPC achieving zero steady-state error and joint-limit safety for physical human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Analytical feedforward cancellation reduces the robot to a constant-state linear double integrator, enabling a fast convex QP with Kalman-augmented disturbance estimation.
card.evaluation: Tested on a 7-DOF Franka FR3 in MuJoCo; outperformed classical impedance with <0.05mm steady-state error under 15N force and sub-millimeter tracking.
card.limitation: Zero-steady-state-error guarantee applies only to constant or asymptotically constant disturbances; anti-windup under persistent saturation is not fully proven.

slides.title: OLIVE: Online Low-Rank Incremental Learning for Efficient Adaptive Exoskeletons
slides.highlight: This work introduces a parameter-efficient online adaptation framework for exoskeleton control, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on adaptive AI coaching and human-AI coadaptation through real-time sensor feedback.

card.one_liner: OLIVE enables real-time, parameter-efficient exoskeleton personalization using low-rank incremental learning and on-body sensor feedback.
card.key_idea: Decomposes control policy updates into low-rank residuals with a gating mechanism for stability and a dynamic rank scheduler to adjust capacity based on terrain complexity.
card.evaluation: Tested with 6 participants across four terrains; outperformed Static, Rule-Based, and Fixed-NN baselines in smoothness, effort reduction, and stability with 7.4ms latency.

slides.title: Individual Gain, Collective Loss: Metacognitive Adaptation in AI-Assisted Creativity
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework of selective metacognitive adaptation to explain how AI use redistributes cognitive effort, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition in human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: AI enhances individual creative satisfaction but reduces collective diversity through selective metacognitive adaptation.
card.key_idea: Routine AI use redistributes metacognitive effort, amplifying partner modeling and surface control while under-supporting originality evaluation, exploratory planning, and reflective integration.
card.evaluation: Theoretical framework synthesizing existing empirical studies on AI homogenization and metacognition; no new empirical data provided.
card.limitation: The framework is not yet empirically validated and primarily draws from text-based writing and ideation tasks.

slides.title: Ouvia: A User-centered Framework for Measuring Usability of Speech Translation in Real-World Communication Scenarios
slides.highlight: Ouvia provides a framework for measuring the usability of speech translation in real-world one-to-one communication, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Ouvia is a user-centered framework measuring the real-world usability of speech translation across diverse demographics.
card.key_idea: A multi-phase protocol involving senders, receivers, and bilingual validators to assess if translations effectively convey key information in healthcare and everyday scenarios.
card.evaluation: 1,738 interactions across four ST systems with speakers of three English dialects. Found QA-based metrics predict usability better than standard automatic metrics.
card.limitation: Limited to one language pair (English-Portuguese) using clean, scripted speech recorded in noise-free environments, potentially overestimating real-world usability.

slides.title: Video2Sim2Real: Full-Stack Autonomous Dexterous Skill Acquisition from a Single Human Video
slides.tldr: AUTONOMOUS DEXTEROUS SKILL ACQUISITION FROM HUMAN VIDEO
slides.highlight: This framework enables autonomous dexterous skill acquisition from human videos by reconstructing digital twins and refining robot motions, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating and transferring procedural skills from ego-exo views.

card.one_liner: Autonomous framework for acquiring robot dexterous skills from a single human video via sim-to-real transfer.
card.key_idea: Reconstructs a digital twin, optimizes robot configurations at object-centric keyframes for trajectory refinement, and uses decoupled IL (geometry) and residual RL (physics) for robust real-world execution.
card.evaluation: Tested on seven everyday tasks; outperformed five RL baselines in simulation (success, safety, smoothness) and achieved 95.7% real-world success rate.
card.limitation: Relies on heuristic keyframe detection, supports only non-articulated objects, and uses sparse keyframe refinement rather than continuous adjustment.

slides.title: Gravity-guided Contact Dynamics Estimation from 3D Human Motions
slides.highlight: GraCE estimates ground contact forces and pressure distribution from 3D motion data, supporting the physics-based human proficiency estimation required for MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: GraCE estimates human ground contact dynamics from 3D motion by leveraging center of gravity guidance.
card.key_idea: A CNN predicts PD controller parameters for total exterior force and gravity-guided contact probabilities based on the distance between body vertices and the center of gravity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on GroundLink (GRF) and MOYO (pressure) datasets; outperformed baselines with a 35.6% increase in vertical ground reaction force accuracy.
card.limitation: Cannot estimate forces when no motion is present and relies on non-deformable SMPL models, making it dependent on motion capture precision.

slides.title: Multi-Turn Evaluation of Deep Research Agents Under Process-Level Feedback
slides.tldr: EVALUATING MULTI-TURN IMPROVEMENT IN DEEP RESEARCH AGENTS
slides.highlight: This research examines how deep research agents respond to process-level feedback and self-reflection, providing insights into the challenges of reliable multi-turn improvement and self-correction relevant to ADAM-CHAT's meta-cognition and adaptation goals.

card.one_liner: Deep research agents improve with process-level feedback but struggle to maintain gains across multiple turns.
card.key_idea: Research Gap Inference (RGI) generates process-level feedback by analyzing rubric patterns to guide agents in adapting search strategies and analytical framing during iterative report revisions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 50 DRACO tasks using normalized scores, pass rates, incorporation, and regression rates.
card.limitation: Current full-rewrite architectures lack structural mechanisms to preserve prior coverage, leading to high regression or excessive computational costs.

slides.title: Agentic AI Co-pilot Platforms
slides.highlight: The emergence of agentic AI co-pilot platforms relates to ADAM-CHAT's focus on developing adaptive AI teammates for human-AI teaming.

slides.title: Dense Force Estimation with an Event-based Optical Tactile Sensor
slides.tldr: DENSE 3D FORCE RECONSTRUCTION VIA EVENT-BASED TACTILE SENSING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for dense 3D force field reconstruction using event-based optical tactile sensors, supporting the physics-based force estimation and high-frequency control needed for MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: First framework for dense 3D force field reconstruction using an event-based optical tactile sensor.
card.key_idea: Combines event-based marker tracking for shear displacements and a U-Net for normal deformation, mapping 3D displacements to forces via the inverse Finite Elements Method (iFEM).
card.evaluation: Tested on a custom dataset with four indenter shapes; achieved MAE of (0.14N, 0.10N, 0.93N) for X, Y, Z forces at 100 Hz.
card.limitation: Linear elasticity assumptions cause errors during large deformations, and limited indenter diversity may restrict generalization.
